candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS LHV Group delivered record financial results in 2024 despite a difficult operating environment marked by a continuing Estonian recession, intense competition for deposits and loans, increased regulatory requirements and falling interest rates during the second half of the year.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Consolidated net income increased 11% to EUR 338.3 million, supported by strong balance-sheet growth, while net interest income rose 8% to EUR 273.3 million and net fee and commission income increased 24% to EUR 60.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Operating expenses grew 14% to EUR 146.9 million, primarily because of higher employee numbers, and expected credit losses increased to EUR 16.3 million from EUR 11.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Nevertheless, pre-tax profit rose to EUR 175.1 million and net profit reached a record EUR 150.3 million, up 7% year on year.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Profit attributable to owners of the parent was EUR 149.0 million, compared with EUR 139.6 million in 2023, while basic earnings per share increased to EUR 0.46 from EUR 0.44.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Growth was concentrated in lending and deposits.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Total assets increased 23% to EUR 8.7 billion, the net loan portfolio expanded 28% to EUR 4.6 billion, and customer deposits grew 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Estonian corporate and retail loan portfolios each increased 21%, while UK SME lending expanded 338% to EUR 348 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Credit quality remained strong overall, although forborne and overdue exposures increased in consumer finance and corporate lending as the economy weakened.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: The Group’s loan-loss allowance rose to EUR 39.8 million from EUR 29.7 million, and a EUR 3.7 million model overlay was recorded for anticipated changes to the ECL methodology.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: LHV Pank remained the main contributor, generating EUR 140.5 million of net profit, slightly below 2023, as higher income was offset by increased operating expenses, credit losses and a EUR 24.4 million deferred tax expense related to anticipated dividends.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: LHV Bank increased net income to EUR 44.6 million and profit to EUR 5.8 million as deposits and lending expanded rapidly, while LHV Kindlustus achieved its second profitable year, with net profit rising to EUR 1.2 million on 21% premium growth.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Asset management profit declined 2% to EUR 1.6 million because no performance fee was earned, while Paytech profit increased 40% to EUR 0.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Profitability remained strong, with ROE at 24.5%, although down from 29.0%, and the cost-to-income ratio at 43.4%.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Capital and liquidity remained well buffered: CET1, Tier 1 and total capital ratios were 16.89%, 17.96% and 20.68%, respectively, while LCR and NSFR were 187.5% and 154.4%.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: The Group issued EUR 300 million of MREL-eligible bonds and EUR 20 million of Tier 2 bonds, while redeeming EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: The share price fell 7% to EUR 3.245, but the proposed 2024 dividend was EUR 0.09 per share.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: For 2025, management expects lower short-term profit because of declining interest rates, partly offset by continued loan growth and efficiency improvements.

factual_claims.claim: AS LHV Group delivered record financial results in 2024 despite a difficult operating environment marked by a continuing Estonian recession, intense competition for deposits and loans, increased regulatory requirements and falling interest rates during the second half of the year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Management Report states: 'Despite the various challenges, 2024 was successful year for LHV. Following a supervisory transition, we managed to restore historically ambitious business growth.' It also mentions 'interest rates are decreasing, competition on lending side has increased drastically... During the full year LHV faced with healthy competition for deposits among banks... Still in very end of the year deposit volumes started to pick up.' The Business Environment section confirms ongoing economic challenges including recession and regulatory pressures.

factual_claims.claim: Consolidated net income increased 11% to EUR 338.3 million, supported by strong balance-sheet growth, while net interest income rose 8% to EUR 273.3 million and net fee and commission income increased 24% to EUR 60.3 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Results section states: 'Net profit was at the historically highest level of EUR 150.3 million (+7% YoY)... Net interest income grew 8% and net fee income increased 24%.' The Financial Results for last 7 years table shows Net income of EUR 338.3 million in 2024 vs EUR 305.5 million in 2023 (11% increase). The breakdown shows Net interest income of EUR 273.3 million (+8% YoY) and Net fee income of EUR 60.3 million (+24% YoY).

factual_claims.claim: Operating expenses grew 14% to EUR 146.9 million, primarily because of higher employee numbers, and expected credit losses increased to EUR 16.3 million from EUR 11.5 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Results section states: 'Operating expenses amounted to EUR 146.9 million (+14% YoY). Most of the increase in expenses has been related to the increased numbers of employees.' The Financial Results for last 7 years table shows Expenses of EUR 146.9 million in 2024 vs EUR 129.4 million in 2023 (14% increase). The same section states: 'Impairments [expected credit losses] amounted to EUR 16.3 million (2023: EUR 11.5 million)'.

factual_claims.claim: Nevertheless, pre-tax profit rose to EUR 175.1 million and net profit reached a record EUR 150.3 million, up 7% year on year.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Results section states: 'The Group's pre-tax profit for 2024 amounted to EUR 175.1 million and net profit totalled EUR 150.3 million (+7% YoY).' The Financial Results for last 7 years table confirms Net profit of EUR 150.3 million in 2024 vs EUR 140.9 million in 2023 (7% increase).

factual_claims.claim: Profit attributable to owners of the parent was EUR 149.0 million, compared with EUR 139.6 million in 2023, while basic earnings per share increased to EUR 0.46 from EUR 0.44.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Results for last 7 years table shows Net profit attributable to owners of the parent of EUR 149.0 million in 2024 vs EUR 139.6 million in 2023. The Ratios table shows Basic earnings per share of EUR 0.46 in 2024 vs EUR 0.44 in 2023.

factual_claims.claim: Growth was concentrated in lending and deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'The loan portfolio increased by EUR 990 million to EUR 4.6 billion (+28% YoY)... The volume of deposits increased to EUR 6.9 billion (+21% YoY)... The increase in the balance sheet volume was driven by growth in deposit base in all customer segments.'

factual_claims.claim: Total assets increased 23% to EUR 8.7 billion, the net loan portfolio expanded 28% to EUR 4.6 billion, and customer deposits grew 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'Total consolidated assets reached EUR 8.7 billion (+23% YoY)... The loan portfolio increased by EUR 990 million to EUR 4.6 billion (+28% YoY)... The volume of deposits increased to EUR 6.9 billion (+21% YoY).' The Overview of LHV Group’s and its subsidiaries’ total assets and net income table confirms these figures.

factual_claims.claim: Estonian corporate and retail loan portfolios each increased 21%, while UK SME lending expanded 338% to EUR 348 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'By the end of December, the total volume of the Group’s net loan portfolio amounted to EUR 4.6 billion (2023: EUR 3.6 billion), an increase of 28%. The portfolio could be divided to three: Estonian corporate banking loans increased by 21% to EUR 2.3 billion (2023: EUR 2.0 billion). Estonian retail loans increased by similar 21%, amounting to EUR 1.9 billion (2023: EUR 1.6 billion). Third pillar is SME loans in UK, the portfolio increased by 338% and reached EUR 0.3 billion.' The LHV Bank section confirms UK SME lending reached EUR 348 million.

factual_claims.claim: Credit quality remained strong overall, although forborne and overdue exposures increased in consumer finance and corporate lending as the economy weakened.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Management Report states: 'The quality of the loan portfolio stayed strong, with some individual customers showing signs of weakening... Overdue loans remained at historically low levels throughout 2024, though there was a slight increase during the year... By year-end, the market average share of loans overdue by more than 60 days stood at 0.3%, reflecting continued stability in the credit market.' The Risk Management section notes increased forborne and overdue exposures in consumer finance and corporate lending due to economic weakening.

factual_claims.claim: The Group’s loan-loss allowance rose to EUR 39.8 million from EUR 29.7 million, and a EUR 3.7 million model overlay was recorded for anticipated changes to the ECL methodology.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial Results section states: 'Impairments [expected credit losses] amounted to EUR 16.3 million (2023: EUR 11.5 million)... The Group fulfilled all the financial ratios published in the initial and in the updated financial plan.' The Risk Management section under Expected Credit Loss Measurement states: 'As of 31 December 2024, a model overlay of EUR 3.7 million was applied to account for the anticipated impact of changes to the ECL estimation methodology planned for 2025.' The allowance for credit losses in the Consolidated statement of financial position increased from EUR 29.7 million to EUR 39.8 million.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Pank remained the main contributor, generating EUR 140.5 million of net profit, slightly below 2023, as higher income was offset by increased operating expenses, credit losses and a EUR 24.4 million deferred tax expense related to anticipated dividends.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The LHV Pank Financial Results section states: 'LHV Pank’s net profit for the year remained almost the same by decreasing just 1% to EUR 140.5 million. Total income increased by 6%, total operating expenses increased by 12%... Credit losses increased by EUR 4.4 million... Results for the year also include EUR 24.4 million deferred tax expense for 2024 payable on the expected future dividend payment.' The Financial Results for last 7 years table confirms LHV Pank's net profit of EUR 140.5 million in 2024 vs EUR 141.4 million in 2023.

factual_claims.claim: LHV Bank increased net income to EUR 44.6 million and profit to EUR 5.8 million as deposits and lending expanded rapidly, while LHV Kindlustus achieved its second profitable year, with net profit rising to EUR 1.2 million on 21% premium growth.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Overview of LHV Group’s and its subsidiaries’ total assets and net income table shows LHV Bank's net income of EUR 44,625 thousand (44.6 million) and net profit of EUR 5,800 thousand (5.8 million) in 2024. The LHV Kindlustus Financial Results section states: 'Net profit for 2024 was EUR 1.2 million... The annual gross written premiums were EUR 38.0 million (+21% YoY)... Net profit for 2024 was EUR 1.2 million.'

factual_claims.claim: Asset management profit declined 2% to EUR 1.6 million because no performance fee was earned, while Paytech profit increased 40% to EUR 0.7 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The LHV Varahaldus Financial Results section states: 'Net profit of LHV Varahaldus was EUR 1.6 million in 2024... Benchmark index growth for 2024 was 6.2%, significantly lower than double digit growth in the preceding two years. While L showed stronger returns in 2024, previous cumulative negative difference must first be remedied before success fee is earned.' The LHV Paytech Financial Results section states: 'Net profit was EUR 0.7 million in 2024, up 40% from EUR 0.5 million in 2023.'

factual_claims.claim: Profitability remained strong, with ROE at 24.5%, although down from 29.0%, and the cost-to-income ratio at 43.4%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Ratios table shows Return on equity (ROE) of 24.5% in 2024 vs 29.0% in 2023. The same table shows Cost to income ratio of 43.4% in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Capital and liquidity remained well buffered: CET1, Tier 1 and total capital ratios were 16.89%, 17.96% and 20.68%, respectively, while LCR and NSFR were 187.5% and 154.4%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Regulatory ratios table shows Common equity Tier 1 (CET1) of 16.89% in 2024, Tier 1 of 17.96% and Total capital adequacy (CAD) of 20.68%. The same table shows LCR of 187.5% and NSFR of 154.4% in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: The Group issued EUR 300 million of MREL-eligible bonds and EUR 20 million of Tier 2 bonds, while redeeming EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Shares and bonds issued by LHV section states: 'In 2024, there was no new share capital issued to the public, except for share options to employees. LHV redeemed EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds and issued EUR 20 million of new Tier 2 bonds... LHV issued EUR 300 million of MREL eligible bonds in May 2024 and concluded a simultaneous voluntary buyback of the 09.09.2025 bond in amount of EUR 137.17 at the same time.'

factual_claims.claim: The share price fell 7% to EUR 3.245, but the proposed 2024 dividend was EUR 0.09 per share.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'LHV share price decreased from EUR 3.495 to 3.245, outperforming the peer group in local market, but not in line with global market trend.' The Allocation of income according to EMTAK section shows the proposed dividend of EUR 0.09 per share for 2024.

factual_claims.claim: For 2025, management expects lower short-term profit because of declining interest rates, partly offset by continued loan growth and efficiency improvements.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Strategy and financial plan section states: 'We enter 2025 in a strong position. Although we anticipate a short-term decline in profits due to changes in the interest rate environment, we can offset part of the negative impact through business growth and more efficient operations.'
